visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 accurately shows the binary search state with the correct mid index/value highlighted and the right search range retained, whereas Lesson 1’s mid-frame has a broken formula with undefined bounds and an incomplete/clipped array visualization.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 1 includes a well-formed quiz gate with a real question, plausible options, a marked correct answer, and a matching gate node wired after act_search_trace, whereas Lesson 2 has no gate specs or plan available, so it provides no functional interactivity.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 1 has clear, natural, well-paced narration with no read-aloud markup or garbling, while Lesson 2 is more rushed as a single dense monologue and ends with an abrupt defective fragment, “Given the sorted array, 3...”.

sync.rationale: Lesson 1 provides generally well-timed visual cues that align with narrated references to targets, pointers, midpoints, comparisons, and discarded halves, whereas Lesson 2 has no beat/timing data or cue triggers, making its visual-narration synchronization absent or unverifiable.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 is more conceptually accurate and pedagogically complete because it explicitly traces low/high/mid updates and derives O(log n) from repeated halving, while Lesson 2 gives a much more compressed trace, loosely says the space is cut “exactly” in half, and does not clearly develop the logarithmic argument beyond assertion.

polish.rationale: Lesson 2 is off-center and cluttered with app UI overlays, but its text and diagrams remain clean and legible, whereas Lesson 1 has more serious polish failures in the mid-lesson frame including clipped array elements and a visibly broken formula showing “undefined.”

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 1 is the clear overall winner: it wins four of six dimensions, all with high confidence, including interactivity, narration quality, synchronization, and conceptual accuracy. These are central instructional dimensions, and the confidence scores for Lesson 1’s wins are consistently strong. Lesson 2 has a strong advantage in visual accuracy and a moderate advantage in polish, reflecting cleaner or more accurate visuals in key frames, but those strengths do not outweigh Lesson 1’s broader pedagogical completeness, functional quiz interactivity, better narration, and better visual-narration alignment.
